title: release.yml validates its window variables before publishing, and PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS uses a real grammar instead of parseInt
description: Found by the LCLI-630 implementer and reviewer (#358, 2026-09-28). LCLI-630 made the post-publish visibility wait refuse a malformed REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS, but the guard fires only AFTER npm publish, so a bad variable fails a release that did publish, and publish:false rehearsals never see it. The reviewer also found a fifth window reader outside the shared grammar: release.yml:1501 passes vars.PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS to release-provenance.mjs, which parses it with parseInt (~line 993): 30m->30, 08->8, 1e3->1, abc throws. Not injectable (quoted node argument). Measured at #358 head 2edab0a3 by the reviewer; no variable is set today (0 repo, 0 release-environment, 0 visible org variables). Also update docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md (~line 800, the LCLI-629 paragraph) to list release.yml as a reader of the window.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release.yml refuses a malformed vars.REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS and vars.PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS BEFORE the first npm publish (and in publish:false rehearsals), naming the variable and showing the value escaped, so a bad variable can no longer fail a release that already published

PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS is validated against the shared REGISTRY_WINDOW grammar (or a stated grammar of its own) instead of parseInt: 30m, 08, 1e3 and abc are refused, proven by tests; the pattern is pinned to its source
The post-publish guard LCLI-630 added stays (defence in depth) or its removal is argued on this task
bun test, lint:shell, actionlint and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the release.yml change

plan: Re-read release.yml and the provenance script and locate the shared window grammar.
Add an always-running job that refuses a malformed REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS or PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS.
Add the same refusal inside the publish job ahead of its first npm publish.
Give the provenance script the shared grammar instead of parseInt.
Write tests that run the real blocks and prove refusals and acceptances for both variables.
Update the release-publishing runbook and run every gate.
implementationNotes: Re-measured the variables 2026-09-28: gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/actions/variables total_count 0; .../environments/release/variables total_count 0; orgs/opum-ai/actions/variables total_count 0. Nothing is set at any level -- the task's measurement reproduces. New measurement: the release environment carries exactly one protection rule -- required_reviewers -- whose only reviewer is jeremy-newhouse.

WHERE THE SHARED GRAMMAR IS: REGISTRY_WINDOW in scripts/promote-latest.mjs (/^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,8})$/) plus pinned window_re literal copies in scripts/publish-release.sh and scripts/readme-readback.sh. release.yml now carries three copies -- the LCLI-630 visibility wait (kept) plus the new release-window job and the publish job's pre-publish step -- and scripts/release-provenance.mjs carries the same literal as WAIT_SECONDS_GRAMMAR replacing the parseInt at --wait-seconds. TWO DESIGN DECISIONS: (1) the always-run release-window job deliberately declares NO environment so a publish:false rehearsal never waits on the required reviewer -- which is why the publish job refuses the environment-resolved REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS itself before its first publish. (2) PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS is checked only at the scope a job without an environment can see because provenance-post (its only reader) declares no environment -- refusing a release-environment value for it would be a red X for a value nothing reads.

MUTATION TESTING -- prediction written before each run. M1 = delete the two refuse_unless_whole_seconds calls in the new job (helpers defined and never called). Predicted 25 red / 39 green. Actual 25 red / 39 green: the red set was exactly the 22 malformed-value executed rows (11 values x 2 variables) plus the bash-arithmetic row plus the both-malformed row plus the CALLS pin. M2 = delete the publish job's whole pre-publish step. Predicted 20 red / 44 green. Actual 20 red / 44 green: exactly the four static pins naming that step plus its 16 executed rows. M3 = restore parseInt at --wait-seconds and leave WAIT_SECONDS_GRAMMAR declared but unused. Predicted 7 red / 57 green. Actual 7 red / 57 green. M3 is the interesting one: the literal pin stayed GREEN as predicted -- a pin on a literal cannot see whether the literal is used -- and the not-toContain-Number.parseInt source assertion is what caught the regression. All three mutants were restored byte-for-byte and the restored tree re-ran green.

GATES at head 334eb026cfcfe152219e11d43a92882731a9e5f5 (working tree clean = the committed tree is the tree every gate ran against): bun test 4612 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail across 129 files and 19188 expect calls; bun run typecheck exit 0; bun run lint exit 0 with 0 errors (4 warnings + 1 info all pre-existing in other files); bun run lint:shell exit 0 (shellcheck 0.11.0 over 8 tracked .sh files); actionlint .github/workflows/release.yml exit 0; bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files / 0 errors / 0 warnings). The new file alone: 64 pass / 0 fail. actionlint is not wired into CI and not in package.json -- it is /opt/homebrew/bin/actionlint 1.x on this machine and was run because the task names it; there is nothing in the repo that would fail if it were absent.

AC4 IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNCHECKED. Its first clause is satisfied and evidenced (all five gates exit 0 at the head SHA above) but its second clause -- a reviewer pass covering the release.yml change -- has not happened yet. The parent session dispatches that review after this implementer returns so the criterion is scored as written and not on its weaker half.

REVIEW OUTCOME AND FIX (2026-09-28, parent). opum-workflow:reviewer returned CHANGES-REQUIRED on origin/fix/LCLI-634-window-validation @ 7e5a1ee7: one REQUIRED finding -- the new suite never pinned continue-on-error or a step-level if, so one YAML key could neuter the gate with all 64 tests green (the reviewer reproduced three variants green; the repo's own rule is that a test that a gate is present is not a test that it can still stop anything). Everything else verified sound: the scope split closes AC1 (one environment: in the file, PROVENANCE_WAIT_SECONDS's only reader declares none), the pre-publish placement is by step order, the grammar is shared and strictly stricter than parseInt, the LCLI-630 guard is intact, and all three mutation results reproduced (25/20/7 red). Its ruling on the flagged trade-off: ACCEPT as shipped. Fix applied by the parent: continue-on-error asserted undefined on the release-window job and each of its steps and on the publish job's new step, if asserted undefined likewise; mutation-proven (job-level continue-on-error -> exactly 1 red; step-level if -> 2 red, the pin and that step's executed row; both restored green). Review finding 3 (comment count word) fixed; finding 2 (CHANGELOG entry) added by the parent. dev merged in: the release.yml conflict resolved as the union the reviewer specified and verified in its own scratch merge (both jobs; needs: [setup, version-parity, release-window, breaking-bump, package, provenance-pre]) -- diff vs dev shows only the LCLI-634 additions, so release.yml at landing is the content the reviewer verified.
